documentTitle: Lê Ngọc Hà · Fullstack Developer · CV
name: Lê Ngọc Hà
headline: Fullstack Developer · Frontend Tech Lead at SAPP Academy

main.heading: Professional Summary
paragraphs: Fullstack Developer, currently Frontend Tech Lead at SAPP Academy, with almost 5 years building web systems for EdTech and TravelTech. Strongest on the frontend (React, Next.js, TypeScript): monorepo architecture, performance, and engineering and security process for the team. On the backend and infrastructure side, I integrated the Payoo POS payment gateway on NestJS, built Spring Boot microservices, and led the move of the dev servers, GitLab and a production database from AWS to CMC Cloud.

entries.title: Hanoi University of Science and Technology

entries.title: Frontend Tech Lead
bullets: Lead the LMS + Ops frontend, review **100% of Merge Requests** and mentor **2 Junior Frontend developers**.
Designed a monorepo with **pnpm Workspace + Turborepo**, brought 4 frontends into it and standardised the shared packages.

Owned the backend integration of the **Payoo POS payment gateway on NestJS** (ops, payment-service, background-job-service): create, cancel and look up orders, IPN handling, a reconciliation cron, HubSpot and SAP sync, **174 test cases**.

Led the move of the dev server (16 NestJS apps), GitLab and the e-contract production database from **AWS to CMC Cloud** in 7 weeks, without renting extra machines; the production database was down for only about **2.5 minutes**.
Upgraded the LMS from **Next.js 12 → 14 App Router** and optimised performance: **page load time down 60% (15.2s → 6.1s)**, Lighthouse **29 → 65+**.
Replaced a commercial editor with **Tiptap**, built as a shared private package, which reduced vendor dependence and licence costs.
Added **Gitleaks, Trivy, Semgrep and OWASP ZAP** to CI/CD and built an AI Workflow: **productivity up 30%**, **~10 hours/week** saved.

entries.title: Fullstack Developer
bullets: Built **5 B2B TravelTech platforms** serving **~1,000 users/month**, plus a multilingual internal admin system.
Built and maintained backend services with **Spring Boot / microservices** in a monorepo.
Optimised SSR and frontend assets: page load 3.2s → 1.1s (-66%), Lighthouse kept at 85.
Mentored **3 Junior Frontend developers** and reviewed Pull Requests before they were merged into Staging.
Restructured and standardised the codebase to make it easier to extend and reuse.

entries.title: Leading with data
text: Prioritised optimisation work on real measurements across 15 pages: **page load time down 60% (15.2s → 6.1s)**, Lighthouse **49 → 67** for the learner pages and **72 → 89** for the instructor pages.

entries.title: Setting engineering standards for the team
text: Set code and security standards, automated the checks in CI/CD and personally review **100% of Merge Requests** — so machines catch the repeated mistakes and people focus on architecture and quality.

entries.title: Mentoring and growing junior engineers
text: Mentored **5 Junior Frontend developers** directly, teaching them how to analyse a problem and find the solution themselves instead of handing them the answer.

entries.title: User-facing performance over server metrics
text: One change cut server response time from 60ms → 3ms on 20 pages. But real measurements showed that users barely noticed the improvement. I decided not to ship it and moved the effort to the bottleneck that does affect the real experience.

entries.title: Merging 4 products into one shared platform
text: The four products used to live in four separate repositories, so shared features had to be built again in each one. I decided to move to a **monorepo with pnpm Workspace + Turborepo**, and to centralise the shared UI, editor and styles.
**Result**: less repeated work, consistent quality, and new products inherit the engineering and security standards straight away.

entries.title: Replacing a paid editor with an in-house one built on Tiptap
text: The old editor was priced per user, so its cost grew with the number of learners. I decided to move to **Tiptap**, and to build it and package it as a shared package in the monorepo.
**Trade-off:** the team owns all development and maintenance of the editor; in return it depends less on a vendor and has better control of long-term cost.
